# std.seq

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Typed lazy sequences. A `Seq<T>` is a reusable description: each
iteration calls `start` for a fresh iterator. Effects happen during
iteration, in order, not when the view is constructed.

## Functions

### `all`

```badger
fn all<T, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, test: fn(T) -> Bool !Eff) -> Bool
```

Whether every item satisfies `test` (stopping at the first that does not).

### `any`

```badger
fn any<T, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, test: fn(T) -> Bool !Eff) -> Bool
```

Whether some item satisfies `test` (stopping at the first).

### `chain`

```badger
fn chain<T, Eff>(a: Seq<T, Eff>, b: Seq<T, Eff>) -> Seq<T, Eff>
```

`a`'s items followed by `b`'s.

```badger
fn chunk_by<T, K, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, key: fn(T) -> K !Eff) -> Seq<List<T>, Eff> where K: PartialEq
```

### `chunks`

```badger
fn chunks<T, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, size: Int) -> Seq<List<T>, Eff>
```

Consecutive groups of `size` items (the last may be shorter).

### `close_iter`

```badger
fn close_iter<T>(it: fn() -> Option<T>) -> Unit
```

Close an iterator's scoped resources now (no-op when it has none or is
already closed). `for` loops call this when they exit early.

### `scan`

```badger
fn scan<T, A, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, initial: A, f: fn(A, T) -> A !Eff) -> Seq<A, Eff>
```

### `scoped`

```badger
fn scoped<R, T, Eff>(open: fn() -> R !Eff, next: fn(R) -> Option<T> !Eff, close: fn(R) -> Unit !Eff) -> Seq<T, Eff>
```

A sequence over a scoped resource. Each iteration calls `open`; the
resource is closed exactly once when iteration is exhausted, when the
consumer terminates early (`break`, `return`, `?`, `take`), or when the
iterating task exits by defect or cancellation.


### `skip_while`

```badger
fn skip_while<T, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, skip: fn(T) -> Bool !Eff) -> Seq<T, Eff>
```

### `step_by`

```badger
fn step_by<T, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, n: Int) -> Seq<T, Eff>
```

Every `n`-th item, from the first (`n` below 1 counts as 1).

```badger

```

### `take`

```badger
fn take<T, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, n: Int) -> Seq<T, Eff>
```

### `take_while`

```badger
fn take_while<T, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, keep: fn(T) -> Bool !Eff) -> Seq<T, Eff>
```

Items while `keep` accepts them; the first it refuses ends the
sequence (and closes the source).

### `try_collect`

```badger
fn try_collect<T, E, Eff>(items: Seq<Result<T, E>, Eff>) -> Result<List<T>, E>
```

The items of a sequence of results, or the first error (the rest are
not produced, and a scoped source is closed).

### `try_each`

```badger
fn try_each<T, E, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, f: fn(T) -> Result<Unit, E> !Eff) -> Result<Unit, E>
```

Run `f` on each item, stopping at the first error (closing a scoped
source).

### `try_fold`

```badger
fn try_fold<T, A, E, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, initial: A, f: fn(A, T) -> Result<A, E> !Eff) -> Result<A, E>
```

Fold in order, stopping at the first error; a scoped source is closed
either way.

### `try_map`

```badger
fn try_map<T, U, E, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, f: fn(T) -> Result<U, E> !Eff) -> Seq<Result<U, E>, Eff>
```

`f` over the items, lazily, as results: `try_collect` (or `try_each`)
then stops at the first error, so later items are never mapped.

### `windows`

```badger
fn windows<T, Eff>(items: Seq<T, Eff>, size: Int) -> Seq<List<T>, Eff>
```

Overlapping consecutive windows of `size` (`size` below 1, or fewer
items than `size`, yields nothing).

### `zip`

```badger
fn zip<A, B, Eff>(a: Seq<A, Eff>, b: Seq<B, Eff>) -> Seq<(A, B), Eff>
```

### `zip_with`

```badger
fn zip_with<A, B, C, Eff>(a: Seq<A, Eff>, b: Seq<B, Eff>, f: fn(A, B) -> C !Eff) -> Seq<C, Eff>
```

Pairs with `other` combined by `f` (as long as the shorter).
